selection_method: Deterministic sentence extraction with minimum length and prose-quality filters, signal scoring, duplicate removal, and per-page concentration limits.

records.public_claim_text: Sweep participants were asked to survey a range of websites in their jurisdiction and to record a response indicating the degree to which products were available for sale, despite: being banned or recalled (“Tier 1”); having inadequate labelling (“Tier 2”); or not meeting voluntary or mandatory product safety standards (“Tier 3”).
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Sweep participants were asked to survey a range of websites in their jurisdiction and to record a response indicating the degree to which products were available for sale, despite: being banned or recalled (“Tier 1”); having inadequate labelling (“Tier 2”); or not meeting voluntary or mandatory product safety standards (“Tier 3”).

records.public_claim_text: More than 4,000 products were inspected in the categories of toys/games, household electrical, household non-electrical, sporting/recreation, apparel, children/infant, and portable technology.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: More than 4,000 products were inspected in the categories of toys/games, household electrical, household non-electrical, sporting/recreation, apparel, children/infant, and portable technology.

records.public_claim_text: The high non-compliance rate suggests that there is room, particularly for online marketplaces and foreign suppliers, to increase their efforts to stay up to date with local recalls, which can be initiated rapidly and may change frequently.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: The high non-compliance rate suggests that there is room, particularly for online marketplaces and foreign suppliers, to increase their efforts to stay up to date with local recalls, which can be initiated rapidly and may change frequently.

records.public_claim_text: While sweepers reported that 47% of products swept had safety information displayed somewhere in the listing, the results point to a need for more and clearer information online.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: While sweepers reported that 47% of products swept had safety information displayed somewhere in the listing, the results point to a need for more and clearer information online.

records.public_claim_text: The 2021 Sweep results thereby confirm that online retailers and marketplaces should further enhance their ability to identify and remove unsafe products from their websites.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: The 2021 Sweep results thereby confirm that online retailers and marketplaces should further enhance their ability to identify and remove unsafe products from their websites.

records.public_claim_text: Many physical stores were moved online for the first time, and many other businesses conducted online or telephone sales exclusively.

records.public_claim_text: Some of these risks potentially require new measures, such as new regulation, better enforcement and business self-regulatory initiatives such as product safety pledges.

records.public_claim_text: Design of the sweep The sweep was coordinated, designed, and implemented by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and the Korea Consumer Agency (KCA).
